title: Django admin and the value of a free back office

videos.script: Every site with data needs somebody to look after it. Fix a typo in a title. Cancel a registration. Find out who signed up. {{need}} In most frameworks that back office is a project of its own. In Django it is one line per model. {{line}} You make a superuser, log in, and register the event model. A list, a search box, forms to add and change rows, and a history of every change, all generated. {{pages}} Then you shape it. The columns an organiser wants, a filter by venue, the registrations inside each event, and an action that downloads them as a spreadsheet. {{shape}} You give Bruno an organiser's account, with a group that lets him change events and only look at registrations. The pages he may not see answer 403. {{bruno}} And then the lesson's warning. Through the admin, a thirteenth person gets into a workshop with twelve seats. The admin writes rows. It does not call your rules. So you decide which doors it may open, and you close the one that bypasses the rule.
